Hi Rory —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our call, I’m sharing a compact integration guide focused on the SDK footprint you asked for: minimal dependencies, straightforward endpoint migration, and a resilient fallback pattern if you hit rate limits during cutover. Attached: redwood-sdk-snippets-v1.zip (single-file SDK + examples).

High-level plan (proposed):
- Staging integration (read-only traffic): 2 days — install SDK, run smoke tests.
- Staging validation: 1 day — run prompt/throughput tests, record latency/cost.
- Cutover window (production): 1–2 hours low-traffic maintenance window.

Key implementation notes inside the attachment, but callouts here:
- SDK boot: single import, configure with API key and region. Example usage in snippets/quickstart.py.
- Retries/timeouts: default client timeout = 10s; retry policy = 3 attempts with exponential backoff (base=300ms) + full jitter.
- Rate-limit handling: SDK surfaces 429 with a structured Retry-After header when available; we recommend an adaptive backoff that respects both Retry-After and internal token bucket throttle.
- Endpoint migration: dual-write pattern for 48 hours to compare responses; SDK has a feature flag (mirror_mode) to send requests to both endpoints and collect diffs.

Can you confirm the staging account details and whether you have a preferred maintenance window? We can put together a day-of checklist for your SRE.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Rory — great questions. Answers inline.

1) Stateful / dual-write guidance: avoid dual-writing mutating ops unless you can guarantee idempotency. For your mutating calls we recommend:
   - Read-dominant paths: mirror_mode ON is safe (the SDK only mirrors and logs responses).
   - Mutation paths: instead of dual-write, run a compare job on a copy: send production writes to primary only but mirror reads and run a nightly diff for the small set of mutating endpoints.
   - If you must dual-write, ensure idempotency keys (we provide idempotency helpers in snippets/idempotency.md) and test with a synthetic replay dataset.

2) Rate limit strategy: start with a conservative guardrail at the infra edge (token-bucket) to prevent burst amplification during cutover — especially if you’re doing parallel replica calls. Keep SDK retries enabled but tune to: max_retries=2, base_backoff=350ms, max_backoff=5s with jitter. SDK will honor Retry-After when present; our servers return Retry-After for quota-based 429s, but not always for transient congestion 429s.

Day-of checklist (abbreviated):
- Pre-cutover: snapshot config + smoke-run (10 sample flows).
- Cutover start: enable mirror_mode for reads, disable any downstream batching that might re-order requests.
- Observe: track 95th/99th p99 latency, error rate, and token consumption.
- Fallback: flip traffic back to old endpoint if errors > 3% for 10m or if p99 latency > 2x baseline.

I attached a migration matrix I use with customers (migration-matrix-20270517.xlsx). I’ll also schedule a 45-minute staging walkthrough on Tue at 09:30 PST unless you want a different time.

Camila
